newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil rig hull off South Australia towed away.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil rig hull off South Australia towed away.

text.p: The hull of a drilling rig disabled during installation off the South Australian coast had been towed to safe anchorage ahead of a repair operation, owner Maersk Contractors said in a statement on Friday.
The company said the hull had been cut away from the rig's three legs, two of which were damaged, and now was anchored in deep water at Port Vincent, west of Adelaide.

It was expected to be brought into Port Adelaide in the next few days, where drilling equipment and damaged sections would be offloaded as a preliminary to towing the rig to a shipyard, probably in Singapore, for major repairs.
Maersk said the three legs of the 8,500 tonnes rig were still to be salvaged, with work expected to begin next week.
A spokesman for the company said there had been no spillage of fuel oils on board as the hull was shifted.

The rig was disabled during installation earlier this month in the first stage of a A$15 million petroleum exploration programme by Canyon, which is 100 percent owned by private Texan based oil and gas explorer and producer Wagner and Brown Ltd.
